paragraphs: In Avodah Zarah 16a: Rav Ashi said, “Zevida (he was an animal fattener) told me: ‘We keep a young ox, and it does the work of two.’” Hyman does not count him among the Torah scholars.

notes.text: The Aramaic describes keeping and fattening an ox; the precise practical scope of “twice as large” in על חד תרין remains to be checked.

The saved whole Davidson Avodah Zarah16a paragraph explicitly asks whether the kept ox grows strong and does work; the saved whole Vilna Rashi scalar glosses על חד תרין as in comparison with other oxen. These resolve the practical rendering as doing the work of two, not becoming twice as large. The selected Rashi scalar does not include the separate fattener lemma; that parenthesis remains Hyman’s text. His Torah-scholar classification remains attributed. The translation-scope question is answered by these texts; the stored source-HOLD classification is retained for a separate explicit clearance gate, not because the twice-as-large rendering remains supported.

Hyman’s print (vol. I, p. 382) gives the heading Zevida and cites Avodah Zarah 16a. Rashi describes Zevida as an animal fattener and explains the comparison as one with other oxen. The passage asks whether the ox regains strength and can work. The young ox does twice the work of other oxen. Hyman gives the classification about Torah scholars.
